cases.answer: Use ResizeObserver because it is faster than a window resize listener and fires before the browser paints anything.
cases.notes: Keyword present, but the stated cause (speed) is not why ResizeObserver is used; the real reason (element vs viewport size) is absent.

cases.answer: You should use ResizeObserver because it is better.
cases.notes: A 'because' with no content is not reasoning.

cases.answer: A window resize event only fires when the viewport changes. A sidebar collapsing or a web font loading can resize a card while the window stays the same size. ResizeObserver reports that element's own size change.
cases.notes: Valid reasoning with no causal keyword (statedReasons is empty).

cases.answer: Put your assertions inside then() because then() retries the whole query chain until the assertion passes.
cases.notes: The bank's listed misconception, stated as the reason.

cases.answer: should() re-runs the query and its assertion until it passes or times out. A then() callback runs one time, and an assertion in it can read the page before it has updated.
Use soft assertions because they are good practice.
